source.title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
source.authors: Zi-Ming Liu; Eric J. Michaud; Max Tegmark

record.tranche_reason: Reports training and test outcomes for supervised networks on MNIST, a different benchmark and setup from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MNIST training outcomes, but does not test the CIFAR, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate, normalization, or label-corruption conditions specified in the versions. Its other grokking results concern different tasks or regression outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study measures delayed generalization and training fit in settings outside the specified versions. Its MNIST models are MLPs, not CIFAR convolutional networks. Initialization comparisons concern generalization delay, without testing activation-matched signal propagation, training speed or trainable depth. Discussion of optimization-oriented initialization cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute grokking to a mismatch between reduced training and test loss landscapes, demonstrate it across several tasks, and attribute its greater dramaticness on algorithmic tasks to stronger dependence on representation learning.
record.recipe_differences: The MNIST experiments use MLPs and nonstandard initialization and data-size choices to study delayed generalization; the paper does not reproduce the claim versions' CIFAR or architecture comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: On MNIST, delayed generalization depends on training-set size and initialization scale; with cross-entropy, the authors report needing a larger initialization scale than with MSE.

fits_no_version.finding: An MNIST ReLU MLP with cross-entropy loss and initialization scale 100 maintains 100% training accuracy while test accuracy improves late.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perfect training accuracy can coexist with delayed generalization in an MNIST MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: An MNIST ReLU MLP trained with AdamW and MSE quickly fits a random 1,000-example subset under enlarged initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A ReLU MLP can rapidly fit a small MNIST training subset under this recipe.

record.problems: The MNIST training-fit claim for the MSE experiment is qualitative, without a numerical training-error value in the text. The paper's experiments are not designed to test the claim versions' specified architectures, datasets, or training conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant MNIST training-fit results were omitted. Other reported results concern test generalization, regression losses, or grokking mechanisms rather than training classification error under a version's conditions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation, training speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Delayed test improvement does not establish slower training optimization under V4. The teacher-student experiment uses a multilayer tanh regression model and does not test V2's architecture or width comparison.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, and the version's model-size and training-recipe comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual depth comparisons, batch normalization, and the cited special-initialization and Fixup conditions.
Matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness trajectories, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: depth-3 width-200 ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with cross-entropy loss and initialization scale α = 100.
rows.note: The paper reports this while test accuracy rises late in training; this is MNIST evidence and does not test the claim versions' CIFAR settings.
rows.check: The reported 100% training accuracy is accurate, but this MNIST MLP result does not measure any specified version. The state is indeterminate relative to those versions.

rows.subject: depth-3 width-200 ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a random 1,000-sample MNIST subset with AdamW, MSE loss, one-hot targets, and initialization scale α > 1.
rows.value: The network quickly fits the training set.
rows.note: The text does not give a numerical training error for this result.
rows.check: Section 4 explicitly reports rapid training-set fit, so the qualitative value is supported. It supplies no numerical training error and concerns an MNIST MLP outside the specified versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
